Rafael / team,

High level technical recommendation (summary):

Option A — Hosted (recommended for speed):
- EU-hosted production cluster (pinned models, EU KV cache + audit logs stored in EU), APAC: dedicated Redwood pool in APAC region.
- Cross-region failover: active-primary routing by region (DNS + routing tier) with EU as secondary for APAC until APAC is fully warmed. During failover session affinity preserved via KV cache replication (async) and fall back to shorter cache TTLs.
- KMS: customer-managed key (bring-your-own-key) in EU for encryption at rest; Redwood holds CMK access policy for cross-region failover events.
- Estimated timeline: EU residency changes (contract + config) — 1–2 weeks; APAC dedicated pool provisioning + validation — 6–8 weeks; full cutover readiness — 8–12 weeks depending on custom integrations.
- Capacity: to meet +60% burst we recommend starting with 2x standard dedicated GPU pools in APAC (N instances) and autoscale policy; EU cluster will need an increase to handle failback headroom (~+20% buffer).

Option B — Private (on-prem / VPC) for EU (higher compliance):
- Deploy Redwood Private in customer-managed EU VPC, with an APAC hosted pool. Longer lead time (12+ weeks) and higher one-time ops fees.

Risks / notes:
- KV cache replication lag can impact session continuity during failover; we mitigate with shorter context window and state reconciliation tooling.
- Certs/KMS cross-region policies require legal signoff if key replication or access is needed.

Deliverables I can produce by 11/10: technical appendix with diagrams, a cross-region failover runbook, and a sizing worksheet to plug in their traffic pattern.

-Vivek
